title: Public Procurement of Innovation
content: Public Procurement of Innovation: Guidelines for government departments to procure innovative solutions from startups outside standard L1 tendering, using pilot-first and outcome-based contracts. This guideline applies primarily to the MobilityTech, GovTech, FinTech for MSME sector(s). Departments and startups engaging in innovation pilots should reference this guidance when structuring procurement, evaluation, or deployment activities. Note: this is illustrative synthetic guidance for a hackathon prototype and does not represent binding government policy.

title: Understanding Technology Readiness Levels (TRL)
content: TRL is a 1-9 scale describing the maturity of a technology, from basic principles observed (TRL 1) to actual system proven in operational environment (TRL 9). Government pilots typically require TRL 4-6 for pilot-stage deployment and TRL 7+ for direct procurement.

title: Cybersecurity Requirements Overview for GovTech Pilots
content: Startups handling citizen or government data should maintain baseline controls: encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access control, audit logging, and periodic vulnerability assessments. CERT-In empanelment or ISO 27001 certification is recommended for higher-sensitivity workloads.

title: Data Handling Guidelines for Pilot Programs
content: Personal or sensitive data collected during pilots must be minimized, anonymized where possible, stored within approved data centers, and deleted per a defined retention schedule after pilot conclusion.

title: Accessibility Requirements for Citizen-Facing Applications
content: Citizen-facing digital services should support screen readers, provide multi-lingual interfaces (including regional languages), and maintain WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for visual and motor accessibility.

title: Sustainability Requirements for Infrastructure Pilots
content: Pilots involving physical infrastructure or hardware deployment should account for energy efficiency, e-waste disposal plans, and, where applicable, use of renewable power sources.

title: Public Procurement of Innovation: Pilot-First Approach
content: Rather than full-scale tendering, departments may run time-boxed pilots (typically 3-6 months) with pre-agreed KPIs before committing to a scaled procurement contract, reducing risk for both parties.

title: Eligibility Screening: Government Experience Weighting
content: Prior government pilot experience is a positive but not mandatory signal. First-time vendors may still qualify if they meet TRL, certification, and deployment capacity thresholds.

title: AI Explainability Requirements for Public Sector Use
content: AI systems used in citizen-impacting decisions should provide human-readable justifications for scores or recommendations, and allow for human review before final action is taken.

title: Vendor Certification Pathways
content: Startups without existing certifications may pursue STQC testing or CERT-In empanelment during the pilot phase, with full certification required before scale-up.

title: Scale Recommendation Criteria
content: A pilot is generally recommended for SCALE when KPI achievement exceeds 80% on primary metrics, for ITERATE when between 50-80%, and STOP when below 50% with no clear remediation path.

title: Sector Compatibility Guidelines for Matching
content: Startups should be matched to challenges within their declared primary or secondary sector to ensure domain expertise, though cross-sector technology transfer (e.g., AgriTech sensors applied to WaterTech) is permitted with justification.

title: Regional Deployment Considerations
content: Startups with only pilot-scale deployment capacity should be paired with single-district challenges, while pan-India capable startups may be considered for multi-state rollouts.

title: Data Retention and Deletion Guidelines
content: Pilot data should be retained only for the duration necessary for evaluation and audit, typically not exceeding 12 months post-pilot-conclusion unless required for a scaled deployment.

title: Innovation Challenge Publication Standards
content: Published challenges should clearly state the problem, required technologies, budget range, and timeline to ensure startups can self-assess fit before applying.

title: KPI Baselining Methodology
content: Baselines should be measured using pre-pilot data over a comparable time period; achievement percentage is calculated as (actual - baseline) / (target - baseline) * 100.
